settings.accordion_title: What's the warranty?
settings.accordion_content:
The Modin Rigid LVP Collection comes with a lifetime residential warranty. The Signature and Craftsman models come with a 20-year commercial warranty. The Base model comes with a 10-year commercial warranty.

Our Silvan Resilient Hardwood Collection comes with a lifetime residential warranty and a 10-year commercial warranty.

You can find all your warranty documents here.

settings.accordion_title: What is the price of each of your products?
settings.accordion_content:
We have three products in our Modin LVP Collection: the Base Collection is $2.95 per square foot, the Signature is $4.50 per square foot, and the Craftsman is $4.95 per square foot.

The Silvan Resilient Engineered Hardwood Collection comes in a7" wide plank and it is $5.50 per square foot.

We also offer matching trim pieces for both the Modin and Silvan Collections.

For the Modin Collection, the T-Molding, End Caps and Reducers are all $35 for 72" pieces. The Quarter Round is $25 for a 72" piece. The matching stair pieces are $40 for the 48" Signature Nosing Square and Round pieces and $40 for the 47" Base Nosing Square and Round pieces.

For the Silvan Collection, the T-Molding, End Caps, and Reducers are all $45 for 78" pieces. The Quarter Rounds are $35. The matching stair pieces are $55 for a 78" piece.

We offer 12" cut samples of any of our products for $3 each, and full planks samples of our Modin Collection products for $20 each. We also offer sample kits for $15 each.

Shipping for any order of 4 boxes or more is a flat $199. For orders of fewer than 4 boxes, shipping is $35 per box. Samples and trim ship for free!

settings.accordion_title: Do you charge sales tax?
settings.accordion_content: We are required to charge sales tax on orders to most states. If your order is subject to sales tax, it will be reflected during checkout. The tax is calculated based on the local sales tax rate associated with your shipping address.

settings.accordion_title: How do holds work?
settings.accordion_content:
We offer unlimited holds (within reason) so you can reserve your floors now and get them when you need them.

When you place your order, leave a note in the "order comments" field indicating that you'd like your order held. Or if you place your order over the phone, let us know that you'd like your order held and we'll make a note on our side.

If you know when you want your flooring delivered, let us know when you place your order. We'll make sure to get your floors to you then. Keep in mind that freight carriers only deliver on weekdays! If your desired delivery date changes, that's okay - let us know and we'll do our best to accommodate you.

Don't know when you will be ready to receive your flooring yet? No problem! If you think you will be ready in the next three months, let us know and we'll set your stock aside. Once you determine when you'll be able to receive your order, contact us -- we just need at least 12 business days notice.

If you think you'll need your floor in more than three months, we can still take your order, but we'll wait to set your stock aside until three months before your need it. So please give us as much notice as possible when you know when you'll be ready to take delivery!

settings.accordion_title: Where can I find your floors locally?
settings.accordion_content:
We are exclusively an eCommerce company which means we don't sell through any distributors or showrooms anywhere in the country.

By going direct to the consumer we have been able to offer the incredibly high-end specs that we have while keeping the price affordable. You'll notice that there is no other brand in any showroom that compares to our specs and the reason for that is that our product would be much too expensive if it went through traditional sales channels.

You can order samples of our product online or give us a call at 1-800-700-8122 and we can help you over the phone.

The samples get mailed to you so that you can see our product in person, take them around your house, and choose a color you love. From there, you can place your full order online, or over the phone with us, and we ship your flooring directly to you.

Check out this short video to learn more about Flooret's business model.

We also offer zero down for 6 months through Paypal Credit.

For commercial accounts, we offer net-60 terms through Resolve. Visit https://app.resolvepay.com/flooret to get preapproved today!

settings.accordion_title: What happens when a color gets archived?
settings.accordion_content:
We're always working to improve our collections and keep them highly curated so, occasionally, we archive a color.

At the beginning of the archiving process, we provide as much notice as possible to existing owners of that color and to those who have ordered samples of the color recently so that they have a chance to order any full boxes they would like of the color.

Once we receive our final shipment of the color that is being archived, we set aside several boxes for our reserve stock of the color. We keep this stock on hand in case any existing owners of the color are in need of a box or two in the future.

When the remainder of the non-reserved stock sells out, the color is officially archived and will generally no longer be available for purchase for orders under 20,000 SF.

settings.accordion_title: How do I get ready for my freight order?
settings.accordion_content:
Watch this video for a quick explanation of how curbside delivery works.

Once your order is scheduled for pick-up by the freight carrier, you'll receive an email with tracking information. Track your order here.

Effortless Shipping and Delivery

At Flooret, we're committed to making the shipping and delivery process as smooth as can be. Trust us to handle your order with care and efficiency, providing you with peace of mind and a great experience from start to finish.

The Shipping Process

We aim to make shipping and delivery a breeze for our valued customers. Once your flooring leaves our warehouse, we'll keep you in the loop with automated tracking updates sent right to your email.We've partnered with reliable carriers who will go the extra mile to keep you informed and make your experience as convenient as possible.

On the day your delivery is scheduled, our carrier will send you emails and even text messages* to let you know when to expect your order at your curb.

Our dedicated drivers take special care of your order and do their best to securely place it curbside.

Carrier Methods: Contactless Delivery or By Appointment
Flooret currently works with a variety of carriers that offer different delivery methods, and each customer is assigned the best carrier to ensure that their order is delivered successfully

Most carriers schedule a delivery window by appointment. You will receive a phone call when the floors arrive to their terminal, and they typically aim to schedule deliveries within the week. You can ask for a window that best fits your scheduling needs.

Currently, the only carrier that offers Contactless Delivery is R&L Carriers. This means you will not be required to be present or give a signature at delivery time. The driver will drop your order off curbside and snap a photo to send to Flooret as confirmation your floors have arrived.

Watch this video for a quick explanation of how contactless delivery works.

Once Your Order Arrives
We want to ensure your complete satisfaction, so we encourage you to inspect each pallet as you normally would. If you notice any damage that may have occurred during transit, no worries! Just take some photos and make a note of the details. Reach out to us at support@flooret.com, and we'll swiftly arrange for replacement boxes if needed.

If you have any questions or concerns about our shipping procedures, our dedicated customer support team is here to help. Feel free to reach out to us anytime. We're always ready to assist you and ensure your satisfaction.

Before you sign for the delivery, inspect the boxes for damage, note it with the driver, and send pictures of any damage to support@flooret.com. Do not refuse the delivery unless there is extreme damage to the entire shipment. Damage doesn't happen often, but if it does occur, we will absolutely make sure that you have the flooring you need to complete your project.

There are written instructions inside the boxes. Please read them carefully.

If you have any questions or need any help along the way, please reach out to us at any time. We're happy to help.

settings.accordion_title: What's your return policy?
settings.accordion_content:
We offer a 6-month return policy and satisfaction guarantee.

At Flooret, we are committed to delivering the highest quality products and providing the best sampling and shopping experience. We are confident you will love your floors. In the unlikely event of product defects, our industry-leading warranties provide you full coverage (please refer to the specific warranty for your floor).

If you receive your order and decide you do not want your floor, we will arrange to have any unopened boxes picked up and returned to us. If returned within 6 months, you will receive a complete refund on your flooring, minus the full cost to ship the product back. If you are returning 4 boxes or more, this qualifies as a freight return and you will need to purchase a Return Kit. This kit will allow you to successfully palletize your flooring and prepare for the carrier to pick it up.

Please note that on your original order you will receive a discounted flat-rate shipping charge, which is not the actual cost of shipping. For your return, you may use your own shipping provider, or we can arrange return shipping using our rates.

To qualify for a return, flooring cannot be installed, cut, damaged, opened, repackaged, or altered in any way. Flooring must have been properly stored in normal living conditions, (between 0°-140°F for the Modin Collection and between 50°-85°F and 40-60% relative humidity for the Silvan Collection) and not have been exposed to the elements. 

NOTE: Original shipping and delivery charges are NOT refundable under any circumstances. All returns must be first authorized by Flooret.

Read our official return policy here for additional details.

settings.accordion_title: How does shipping work?
settings.accordion_content:
While ordering flooring online and receiving it at your home or business may seem daunting, we’ve taken steps to ensure that the process is as easy as possible.

After you place your order, our warehouse personnel will safely and securely package your order with durable materials and prepare it for pickup. Once picked up at our warehouse, the carrier will generate a tracking number that will be emailed to you.

Depending on your location, we will either book your order as a Contactless Delivery or a By Appointment Delivery.

If your order is shipped with FedEx Freight, Old Dominion Freight Lines, or XPO Logistics, you’ll receive a phone call from the carrier 24 hours prior to delivery to schedule a delivery appointment that works for you. Someone will need to be present to sign for the delivery.

Watch this video to get a better idea of how a By Appointment Delivery works.

If your order is shipping with R&L Carriers, your order will be delivered to your curb even if no one is present to sign for it. R&L Carriers will email and text you on the day your order is scheduled for delivery to your address. The driver will deliver your flooring order, cover the pallets if inclement weather is expected, photograph the delivery, and be on their way.

Watch this video to get a better idea of how a Contactless Delivery works.

Don’t need your floor right away? Let us know at the time of the order and we can hold your floors until you’re ready for them.

Things to Keep in Mind

  • A curbside freight delivery means a much larger truck than you’re probably used to seeing. Let us know ahead of time if you think your curb might be difficult for such a large vehicle to access
  • The driver will remove the pallets from the truck but is not required to bring anything inside for you so remember to have help on the day of the delivery
  • In the rare event that your shipment is damaged during transit, please note the damage when signing for the delivery and contact us at support@flooret.com so that we can resolve the issue immediately

settings.accordion_title: Do you ship to Alaska and Hawaii?
settings.accordion_content:
Yes, through a freight forwarder of your choice.

A freight forwarder is required to ship freight to Alaska and Hawaii. We can recommend a freight forwarder to you if you need one.

Our flat-rate $199 shipping charge covers shipping to a forwarder. From there, the forwarder will continue shipping your order to its final destination.

Once you've selected your forwarder, you will need to coordinate with them to arrange your shipment. We'll need to know which forwarder you are using and their shipping address. Your forwarder will likely require shipment information like pallet dimensions, pallet weight, and freight class.

Our Shipping Team can provide freight forwarder recommendations as well as any shipment information you need. You can reach them by emailing support@flooret.com or by calling 1-800-700-8122.

settings.accordion_title: Do you ship to Canada?
settings.accordion_content: While we have had some customers successfully receive our product in Canada, the process is quite onerous, as we do not ship directly to Canada. On top of needing to find a freight forwarder that will ship to your area, we would recommend retaining a customs broker to help you with the process. We are hoping to expand into Canada in the future, but don't have a timeline on that yet. Please reach out to support@flooret.com if you have any questions!

settings.accordion_title: Will the product be delivered inside my house?
settings.accordion_content:
No, your floors will be delivered curbside only. The delivery truck will have a lift-gate to allow the driver to remove the pallet(s) from the back of the truck in a safe location in front of the property. The driver is not required to bring the floors into the property for you.

For more information on how your flooring delivery will work, please watch this helpful video.

settings.accordion_title: How do I get samples of your products?
settings.accordion_content:
You can order samples directly on our website, through live chat with an agent, or over the phone at 1-800-700-8122.

As an eCommerce company, we don't have any showrooms or distributors, which is why we're able to offer such high-quality specs at such a low cost. Instead of driving to a flooring store in your area to see samples, we ship our samples directly to your doorstep so you can see the product in your own home.

We offer 12" cut samples for $3 each and full plank samples for $20. Shipping is free for samples. The 12" cut samples arrive in 2 business days and the full planks samples take 5-7 business days.

If something does happen to be out of stock, we'll let you know right away and get you your samples as soon as possible.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Transitions and Trim pieces
settings.accordion_content:
We offer a full range of matching transition pieces, including T-moldings, End Caps, Reducers, Quarter Rounds and Stair Pieces.

To find the transition or trim piece you need, navigate to the product page of the color you are looking for. Scroll down to the section titled “Buy Transitions” and press the right arrow button to scroll through all the transition pieces available for that color. If you are looking for a specific piece, you can also use the search feature located on the top right corner of any page of our website.

The T-molding is used to transition between two floors that are the same height.

The Reducer is designed to "reduce" down from our planks to the subfloor. Modin Reducers can be adapted to transition between any two floors that differ in height by about 1/4".

We would recommend using the End Cap if you plan to run the floor up against something like a fireplace hearth or sliding door where you won't be able to hide the expansion gap with a baseboard or quarter round.

The Quarter Round is a perimeter piece that is used to cover the expansion gap when a baseboard cannot be used. If you are not removing your baseboards before installing our planks, you will need to leave the recommended expansion gap between the planks and the baseboards, and cover this with shoe molding or quarter rounds. Keep in mind that our quarter rounds match the color of our floors. Many people prefer to use plain, white quarter rounds that are available at local hardware stores.

If you are not sure which transition piece is most suitable for your installation, we recommend watching this helpful video on our YouTube channel, for more information.
​​​​​​​​​
And here is a demo on how to install each of those transition pieces:

  • End Cap
  • Reducer
  • T-Molding
  • Quarter Round

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Can I add an additional underlayment?
settings.accordion_content:
Our planks come with a pre-attached underlayment and is designed to install directly over your existing flooring or subfloor, without any additional underlayment.

The IXPE foam underlayment that comes pre-attached to our planks already has an excellent sound insulation rating (up to IIC 64 / STC 62) and contributes to the floor feeling soft underfoot. An additional, soft, underlayment that is more than 3mm thick would void the warranty, as it has the potential to put too much strain on the click mechanism. If you do choose to use an additional underlayment, we recommend sticking with something 1-2mm thick. Make sure to use an underlayment that is approved for use with LVP planks.

A moisture barrier is required if you are installing on a concrete slab. We recommend using a simple 6 mil thick polyethylene moisture barrier, which should be available at your local hardware.

If you're looking to raise your subfloor, it's better to use approved subfloor materials such as luan, plywood, or self-leveling concrete.

Watch this helpful video about why an additional underlayment is not necessary.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Do I need a moisture barrier?
settings.accordion_content: In most cases, a moisture barrier is not necessary for the sake of the flooring itself, as the Modin Collection is 100% waterproof. A moisture barrier is required if you are installing the flooring on a concrete slab, though. Using a moisture barrier will reduce the humidity in your space, prevent mold and mildew growth, and helps prevent rare issues that can arise as a result of excess moisture building up underneath the planks. We recommend using a simple 6 mil thick polyethylene moisture barrier, which should be available at your local hardware store.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | What installation tools will I need?
settings.accordion_content:
We recommend using the following tools to complete your installation of Modin LVP:

  • Miter Saw
  • Table Saw (most precise for cutting planks lengthwise)
  • Tape Measure & T Square
  • Universal tapping block
  • Pull bar
  • Heavy mallet
  • Straight Edge & 1/4” Spacers

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Do you have a solution for stairs?
settings.accordion_content:
Yes. We offer Stair Nosing made from real planks for each of our products, as well as hollow PVC full treads, and a 72" budget-friendly overlapping stair nose. The Stair Nosings are available in the 48" Signature Nosing Square and Round pieces and the 47" Base Nosing Square and Round pieces. The Base Stair Nosings are only compatible with the Base planks, but the Signature Stair Nosings are compatible with the Craftsman planks as well as the Signature planks. They can be used in combination with planks to complete a staircase.

This video shows how to install the Stair Nosings.

If you're using planks as matching risers, start at the bottom of your staircase. If you're not using risers, you can start from anywhere (some customers opt to paint their risers white or some other unique concept).

To begin, install the first riser. You may need to trim the height of the riser to match the height of your step. Sand the back of the riser and lay strips of glue on the back of the riser approximately 6-inches apart. Press the riser into place and use painter's tape to hold the riser in place while you prepare for the next step.

Cut a stair nosing and Modin plank to fit your step. You may need to cut away any existing bullnose unless the stair nosing fits over it. Once your pieces are the right size, interlock the stair nosing and the plank to form a full tread, remove the painter's tape from the previous step, and apply adhesive to the nosing and plank despite the fact that they are interlocked with one another. Press the pieces onto the stair.

On the next step, the riser will now sit on top of the tread piece so you may need to cut it shorter than you did for the first step.

Repeat these steps until you reach a landing or the top of your staircase.

Installing on landings and at the top of the staircase

Installing on landings will be the same as the other stairs except that you'll need more than one plank to cover the entire step.

For the top edge of the staircase you will likely need to cut off the click mechanism of the stair nosing so, when installed, it will sit flush with the neighboring plank(s).

Measure the distance needed to accommodate the nosing and draw a line on your subfloor, or on top of the planks if that level of the house has already had the floors installed to the edge of the staircase. If the planks were installed to the edge, you'll need to cut them back at the line you just placed. Now the stair nosing can be glued down to complete your stair installation. You'll need to use adhesive under both the nosing and the adjacent plank(s). This will prevent any gaps from forming between your planks and the stair nosing.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Can my flooring be installed over radiant heat?
settings.accordion_content:
Yes. Modin Rigid Plank can be installed over in-floor radiant heating systems provided the subfloor surface does not exceed 85°F at any point.

If installing on top of a new radiant heat system, make sure the new system has been active for at least 48 hours. Some radiant systems will have a temperature "spike" the first time they are used.

The initial floor temperature should not exceed 70°F for 24 hours prior to and 48 hours after installation. Thereafter the temperature should be gradually increased to the desired setting, up to but not to exceed 85°F. Radiant heating systems that are installed on top of the subfloor surface and covered with self-leveling underlayment are not recommended. Modin Vinyl Plank may be installed over gypsum-based underlayments.

Electric heating mats that are not embedded into the subfloor are not recommended for use underneath Modin Rigid Vinyl Plank. Although some of these may work, in rare cases these mats can overheat and cause the underlayment to melt. If in doubt test a couple of planks before placing your entire order.

Watch this video to learn more about installing your flooring over radiant heat!

settings.accordion_title: Modin | How do I transition between two floors that are the same height?
settings.accordion_content:
The T-molding is used to transition between two floors that are the same height.

Watch this video to learn more about the installation process.

Before installing the T-molding, you will first want to make sure that the space left for the T-molding allows for the recommended ¼ inch expansion space between the track and the floor on either side of the track. This means leaving approximately a 1 ¼ inch gap between the two adjacent floors where the T-molding will be installed.

When you are ready to install the T-molding:

  • First cut the T-molding and track to the desired size using a power saw. ​​
  • Separate the track from the T-molding.
  • Lightly sand the bottom of the track. This will help the adhesive bond more effectively. ​​
  • Apply a general construction adhesive to the track and glue it down.
  • Once the glue is set, insert the T-molding into the track, starting on one side and working your way to the other side. Use a mallet to tap it firmly in place.
    ​​​​​​​

If you are not sure which transition piece is most suitable for your installation, we recommend watching this helpful video on our YouTube channel, for more information.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | How do I transition between LVP and carpet?
settings.accordion_content:
Method 1: No Transition

Instead of using a transition piece where the two floors meet, pull the carpet tight and wrap the edge underneath. This will hide the unattractive cut edge of the carpeting. You can use staples or whatever method your professional installer recommends to hold the carpet down.

Slide the edge of your vinyl floors underneath the curved edge of the carpeting to create a seamless transition.

Method 2:T-Molding

Sand the bottom of the t-molding track and lay down a strip of glue at the edge of the carpet. Place the track so that the edge of it slides underneath the tack strip at the edge of your carpeting. You want the edge of the carpeting to go over the edge of the track.Install your vinyl floors up to the other edge of the track and snap in the t-molding, hiding the edge of both the carpet and the vinyl.Watch this video to learn how to install a T-Molding.

Method 3:End Cap

Install your vinyl floors up to the carpeting until you reach a distance that can be covered by the end cap (roughly 1/2 - 3/4"). Sand the base of the end cap, lay a strip of glue, and press the end cap in place.

Wait for the glue to dry, then tuck in the edge of the carpeting and trim off any stray fibers with a utility knife.

Watch this video to learn how to install an End Cap.

If you are not sure which transition piece is most suitable for your installation, we recommend watching this helpful video on our YouTube channel, for more information.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | How do I install a Reducer?
settings.accordion_content:
Watch this helpful video to learn how to install a Reducer.

We offer Reducers that can be used to transition between two floors that differ in height by about 1/4".

The Reducer is 72 inches long and is available in all colors to match your floor. When you order a Reducer, it will come with a track and the Reducer itself.

The Reducer is designed to transition between your Flooret floor and your subfloor. It can also be used to transition between two floors that differ in height by about ¼”.
​​​​​​​​​​​
For example, if you will be ending your Flooret floor at the door to your garage and need to transition down to the concrete subfloor, you can use the Reducer.
​​​​​​​​​​​
If you are transitioning between 1/2" tile in your bathroom and Flooret planks in your hallway, you can also use the Reducer.
​​​​​​​​​​​
Before installing the Reducer, you will first want to make sure you are leaving the recommended expansion space. If you are transitioning from your Flooret floor to the subfloor, you will simply need to leave about ¼” between the track and the edge of the floor.
​​​
If you are using the Reducer to transition between two floors, you will need to leave the recommended ¼ inch expansion space between the track and the floor on either side of the track. This means leaving approximately a 1 ¼ inch gap between the two adjacent floors where the Reducer will be installed.
​​​​​​​​​​​
When you are ready to install the Reducer:

First cut the Reducer and track to the desired size using a power saw.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Can I install this floor in a 3-season room?
settings.accordion_content: Modin is warrantied for indoor use within temperatures of 0-140F. If your 3-season room stays within those limits it is fine to use. Keep in mind that although Modin does have a UV-protective coating, direct sunlight can still fade the floors over time. Using curtains or UV-protective windows in a 3-season room will help slow that process.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | How do I store my flooring?
settings.accordion_content: Keep cartons stored horizontally at all times. Stacking them vertically will damage the click mechanism. During storage, Modin planks can withstand temperatures between 0-140 ºF. They do not require acclimatization.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | How long does the floor need to acclimate before it is installed?
settings.accordion_content: Unlike standard vinyl plank and WPC products, the Modin Collection does not require acclimation prior to installation due to its incredibly stable SPC core.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Can I install cabinets on top of my flooring?
settings.accordion_content:
It is always recommended to install cabinets before floating flooring rather than installing cabinets on top of floating floors.

We recommend installing cabinets before your floors when installing a floating floor like the Modin Collection. This lowers the risk of your floor failing in the future.

While most modern cabinetry is unlikely to cause issues even if it is installed on top of the floor, out of an abundance of caution, we recommend installing the cabinetry first and leaving the industry-standard 1/4" of expansion space between the floor and the cabinetry.

Appliances are not a concern; you can safely place those on top of your floor.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Can I install my flooring over an existing floor?
settings.accordion_content:
Modin planks can be installed over a variety of finished floors including single-layer resilient sheet floor and tile, ceramic, marble, and terrazzo.

The surface must be in good condition and show no signs of excessive moisture conditions. If the existing floor is warped or damaged, or shows signs of mold, this could indicate moisture is coming up from the sub-floor, and installing Modin on top can lead to this moisture getting trapped and warping the existing floor, or causing the existing floor to mold and rot further. Remove the existing floor and test the subfloor moisture levels.

Do not install flooring over heavily cushioned floors or over tile installed over concrete below grade level. The grout joints in ceramic tile and marble must be leveled so they are flush with the tile surface. Additionally, the tile may require several skim coats to achieve a flat surface.

Thinking of installing over existing wood or laminate floors? Wood floors and laminate floors are very sensitive to moisture. By installing Modin Rigid on top of these floors, you risk moisture from the sub-floor getting trapped and accumulating. This can cause the wood and laminate floors to warp underneath your new flooring. This is less of a concern if your existing floor is on a second story or over a crawl space, but if the existing floor is installed directly over a slab it is always safer to remove the floor and go directly down on the slab.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Do I need to leave expansion space when installing my LVP?
settings.accordion_content:
While our planks are more dimensionally stable than other LVP products due to their rigid SPC core, you will need to leave the industry-standard 1/4" of expansion space between your floor and anything it is running up against.

Our planks are made with a very robust stone polymer composite (SPC) core. Luxury vinyl planks that feature an SPC core expand and contract much less than LVP products made with less sophisticated core materials. Out of an abundance of caution, we still require that you leave the industry standard 1/4" of expansion space when installing your floor. While your floor may not expand or contract much itself, keep in mind that the rest of your home does.

Problems typically only occur in situations where a number of factors combine to put excessive pressure on the planks. Sustained direct sun exposure and a very long run can lead to expansion-related problems if expansion space is not left. If you choose to forego expansion space in some areas, you may not run into any issues, but any problems that do arise would not be covered under our warranty.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | How flat or level do I need my subfloor to be?
settings.accordion_content:
For our Modin Collection, the official recommendation for subfloor flatness is that any imperfections should not exceed 3/16" over 10'.

More than levelness, "flatness" is a much more important factor. In other words, if your entire room slopes in one direction, but is otherwise flat the entire way, your installation can be successful.

For our Modin Collection, the official recommendation for subfloor flatness is that any imperfections should not exceed 3/16" over 10'. That being said, we have had many customers tell us they have installed on considerably less flat surfaces. There are three primary concerns with the subfloor not being flat.

The first is that the click mechanism may come loose. If the subfloor changes angle too dramatically in the middle of a plank, the pressure over time may lead to the click mechanism breaking or coming loose.
The second concern is telegraphing. Precisely because vinyl floors are malleable, you can have imperfections in the subfloor telegraph to the surface and be visible.

The final concern is hollowness. When a plank bridges a valley, the hollow spots can result in the floor sounding soft or "loose" wherever there are air pockets between the floor and the subfloor.

Checking for flatness prior to your installation is the most important step you can take for a successful install.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Can I install these planks outdoors?
settings.accordion_content:
No. Our floors are designed for indoor use only.

Modin LVP, like all vinyl plank flooring, is designed to be installed in temperature and moisture controlled indoor environments.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | What can I do to minimize or avoid repeating patterns?
settings.accordion_content:
Have 2-3 boxes open at a time while installing so you can choose from a nice range of planks and make sure repeating planks are as far apart as possible.

Here is a helpful video to walk you through the process.

Every vinyl floor eventually repeats its pattern. To minimize having two planks that are identical right next to each other, it is important you become familiar with the pattern you are installing and look for conspicuous patterns that will catch the eye. We recommend having 2-3 boxes open at a time, so you can pick a nice range of planks.

Also, make a point of standing up every few planks and taking a larger view of your floor, especially when installing near "focal points" (areas like entryways where individuals are more likely to inspect the floor). This will help you catch repetition that you may have missed while down on your knees.

The print film gives your floor its distinct look. With print film manufacturers now carrying catalogs that number in the thousands, you can get virtually any design you can imagine. While there is no accounting for taste and trends, there are some objective details to consider with print design.

Most print films come in a set size, usually 40” by 52" wide. Out of this print film, planks are cut at random points, leading to a certain set of patterns. The degree of variation between planks is referred to as the “repeat pattern.” Although there is some degree of flexibility on the size of the print a company can use, in general, this size is pretty set, leading to repeating patterns every 15 SF or so.

There are a few things to keep in mind that can help reduce repeat patterns. The first is to pick a pattern that doesn’t have overly distinct features. The more distinct the grain or texture in the print film, the more obvious it will be when that distinct pattern reappears.

Secondly, it is important to be mindful during the installation of the floor what planks go next to each other. It is best to have 2-3 boxes open at a time and to make sure repeating planks are as far apart as possible.

Third, ask how long the original print film is. Most manufacturers don't advertise this, but you want a print film that is at least the length of the planks. For example, Modin Rigid has 72" print films, meaning the pattern does not repeat within the same plank. This is not the case with other brands carrying 72" planks, so it is important you look out for this.

One more note to consider with your print pattern is how “wearable” the pattern is. Floors inevitably get dirty as they get walked on, and some colors and patterns will show dirt more than others. Especially with very light or white floors, it is worth seeing if the pattern has enough of a weathered look that dirt will hide. You will notice in our Modin Collection that our lighter colors have a wire-brush look that has a more weathered appearance, in order to better hide actual dirt. A completely uniform white floor might look more modern at first glance but will quickly look dirty. The same can apply to extremely dark floors as well.

settings.accordion_title: Does Flooret provide installation services?
settings.accordion_content:
While we don't offer installation services through Flooret, we are happy to recommend an installer in your area whom we think will do a great job.

We have a growing database of installers who have worked with our product before. However, previous experience installing our floors is not necessary to successfully install this flooring.

We are happy to connect you with someone from our network of qualified installers. To request an installer, email our team at support@flooret.com or call our team at 1-800-700-8122.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | What is the best cleaner to use on my floors?
settings.accordion_content:
Any products that are safe to use on vinyl floors will be suitable. We recommend Bona Luxury Vinyl Floor Cleaner or any similar brand. Make sure to avoid products that contain wax, as that will build up over time.

You may wet mop your floors as much as needed; the planks are 100% waterproof. We do not recommend using steam cleaners, though. Steam cleaners can dull the floor with repeated use, so if you do want to use a steam cleaner, do so sparingly and at a lower temperature setting.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | How do I care for my floor?
settings.accordion_content:
Keep your floors clean, use felt protectors on furniture, avoid direct exposure to intense sunlight, and refrain from using products with wax or "shine" agents.

After installing the floor, we recommend an initial cleaning to remove any loose dirt or debris that may have been introduced during the installation process. While most non-residue cleaners can be used on your vinyl plank floors, it is always recommended to conduct a small test patch in an inconspicuous area, and avoid using harsh cleaners or ammonia-based cleaning products.

Keep Floors Clean
Regularly sweep and vacuum your floors. Dust acts as an abrasive. Keeping your floors dust-free will prolong the life of your finish and wear-layer. Use a vacuum that is suitable for hard surface floors.

Use walk-off mats at outside entrances to reduce the amount of dirt brought into your home.

Do not wax your vinyl flooring, or use any “mop and shine” products. The surface of your floor is very dense and nonporous, which prevents wax from penetrating and thus builds up a bed for yellowing and dirt collection. The same non-porous feature also provides all the protection against wear and staining that you will need. Watch this helpful Instagram Reel to learn more about how to keep your floors clean.

Furniture
When moving appliances or heavy furniture, we recommend laying a Masonite panel on your floor for the best protection.

Use felt protectors on furniture to reduce indentation. As a general rule of thumb, the heavier the item, the wider the floor protector is needed. We recommend felt pads at least 1” in diameter.

Be careful with rolling casters. They can damage the floor. If you choose to use them, look for the widest possible wheel you can find. Watch this helpful Instagram Reel to learn more about how to protect your floors from furniture damage.

Sunlight Exposure
The Modin Rigid Collection has a UV protective coating on top of the wear layer which dramatically slows possible fading from sunlight.

To keep your floors in pristine condition, avoid exposure to direct sunlight for prolonged periods of time. During peak sunlight hours, use drapes or blinds to minimize the direct sunlight on the vinyl flooring. Most types of flooring will be affected by continuous strong sunlight. In addition, excessive temperatures are not good for resilient floors.

Some natural ventilation or intermittent air conditioning in vacant homes should be considered.

Long-term continuous inside temperatures over 115°F combined with strong direct sunlight will damage the flooring and cause the installation to fail. Watch this helpful Instagram Reel to learn more about how to protect your floors from sunlight damage.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Will sun exposure damage my floor?
settings.accordion_content:
The Modin Rigid Collection has a UV protective coating on top of the wear layer which dramatically slows possible fading from sunlight.

To keep your floors in pristine condition, avoid exposure to direct sunlight for prolonged periods of time. During peak sunlight hours, use drapes or blinds to minimize the direct sunlight on the vinyl flooring. Most types of flooring will be affected by continuous strong sunlight. In addition, excessive temperatures are not good for resilient floors

.Some natural ventilation or intermittent air conditioning in vacant homes should be considered.

Long-term continuous inside temperatures over 140°F combined with strong direct sunlight will damage the flooring and cause the installation to fail.

Watch this helpful Instagram Reel to learn more about how to protect your floors from sunlight damage.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | Can I use a steam mop on my floor?
settings.accordion_content:
All of the designs in the Modin Collection are 100% waterproof and include a tough top coating. However, using a steam mop on our floors can, over time, dull the finish. If you do choose to use a steam mop, do so only occasionally to avoid dulling the finish. Additionally, you can steam at half-power and at a lower steam setting.

Other, lower quality, luxury vinyl flooring products react quite badly to steam mops, bending and warping along the edges in response to the high heat, but Modin planks won’t be damaged in this manner by a steam mop.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | How do I repair a scratch in my flooring?
settings.accordion_content:
Our collections come with top-notch scratch-resistant coatings and are built with an industry-leading, 100% virgin PVC wear layer, but accidents can happen and in the event you get a scratch on your flooring, there are a couple ways you can repair it.

Watch this helpful video on how to repair a scratch on your LVP.

How to Prevent Scratches

  1. Keep your floors clean - Regularly sweep and vacuum your floors. Dust acts as an abrasive. Keeping your floors dust-free will prolong the life of your finish and prevent micro-scratches.
  2. When moving appliances or heavy furniture, we recommend laying a Masonite panel on your floor for the best protection.
  3. Use felt protectors on furniture to prevent scratches when moving. As a general rule of thumb, the heavier the item, the wider the floor protector needed. We recommend felt pads at least 1” in diameter.
  4. Be careful with rolling casters. They can damage the floor. If you choose to use them, look for the widest possible wheel you can find.

How to Repair a Scratch

  1. Buff it out - You can do this with a microfiber cloth or the back of a spoon. You can also try using a damp cloth to rub out scratches.
  2. Repair it - For deeper scratches, we recommend a scratch repair product to our Modin Collection customers. There are numerous products on the market but here is an example of one: Wearmax Scratch Concealer.
  3. Replace it - For very deep scratches, you may consider replacing the affected plank. Take a look at this video, which shows how to do this.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | How do you replace a plank?
settings.accordion_content:
If needed, you can replace a Modin plank in the interior of your installation.

Take a look at this video, which does a great job of showing how to replace an LVP plank.

Here are the step-by-step instructions:

Carefully remove the damaged plank.

  • Use a ruler or a straightedge to draw a line in the center of the plank.
  • Next, draw 45-degree lines from all the corners to the center line, forming a triangle on each end of the plank.
  • To avoid damaging the subfloor, adjust the depth of your saw blade to match the thickness of the plank.
  • Use the saw blade to carefully cut through the centerline of the plank, stopping at the beginning of each triangle.
  • Sweep or vacuum up the debris.
  • Now, cut through the diagonal lines taking care not to cut any adjacent planks.
  • Remove the central sections, then each of the triangle-shaped sections.
  • Use a small sharp chisel to remove the lock mechanism from the long and short edges of the surrounding planks.
  • Make sure the area is completely clean.

Next, prepare the new plank.

  • Use a sharp chisel to remove the lock mechanism from the long and short edges of the plank
  • Cut the corners where the two grooved edges meet using a utility knife.
  • Apply adhesive to the exposed grooves on the replacement and adjacent planks.

Now you are ready to install the new plank.

  • First, align the cut corner, sliding the exposed click mechanism underneath the sides of the adjacent planks, and then drop the plank into position.
  • Use a rubber mallet to firmly tap the plank into place until it is entirely flat.
  • Wait for the adhesive to fully set, and your plank replacement is complete!

settings.accordion_title: Modin | What rugs and rug pads can I safely use with my floors?
settings.accordion_content:
Look for rugs that are non-staining or labeled as "colorfast" or "safe for use with hardwoods". Avoid rubber and latex mats if possible.

Regarding rugs, it is best to use non-staining vinyl-backed mats or any rug that is labeled as "colorfast." Area rugs that say "Safe for Use with Hardwoods" should be just fine. You can look at rugs with natural backings, such as cotton, jute, and woven backings.

As is the case for all vinyl floors, in some cases, plasticizers in rubber and latex can react with our planks in ways that discolor the flooring. We haven't tested our floors with every type of plasticizer, so we would recommend checking with the manufacturer of the product to be sure that it is compatible with vinyl flooring. If it is safe to use with vinyl, it is safe to use with our floor.Most non-slip pads that are recommended for hardwood floors are a safe choice for vinyl plank. The kind to avoid, which is rarely found these days, is the old plastic mesh type, which has a tendency to leave a residue in hot temperatures. Any kind of foam pad should be fine, however. We have included a link below to some worry-free pads so that when you find a rug you love, you don't have to think about the backing!

https://www.rugpadusa.com/collections/for-vinyl-and-vinyl-plank-floors

What about Ruggable?

We reached out to Ruggable to ask them about the construction of their rugs and backings. They told us that their latex-free TPR backing material has passed all flooring tests and does not stain or leave residue on hard surface floors (including concrete). Based on that information, Ruggable rugs are safe to use with Flooret floors.

settings.accordion_title: Modin | What do I do if my house experiences flooding?
settings.accordion_content:
The Modin Collection is waterproof, but if water gets under the planks, you will need to uninstall the planks, dry them and the area thoroughly, and reinstall them.

If your floor has been exposed to excessive amounts of water due to flooding, do not panic; our Modin Collection is 100% waterproof. If the water did not reach the perimeter of the installation, simply remove the water as quickly as possible.

Depending on the extent of the flooding, you may need to uninstall parts of the floor to allow the sub-floor to dry out. This is possible with the click products like Modin. Carefully uninstall the boards, taking care to not damage the click mechanisms so that you can re-install later. Before reinstalling the planks, dry them and the area thoroughly using a water pump, fans, and a dehumidifier.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | Do I need to use an underlayment or moisture barrier?
settings.accordion_content:
A moisture barrier is required, and an underlayment is recommended for floating installations

If you are planning to install your Silvan flooring using the glue-down method, you will not need an underlayment, but you will need to use the Bona R590 (or equivalent) liquid moisture barrier.

If you will be installing it as a floating floor, you will need a moisture barrier (a 6 mil polyethylene moisture barrier is perfect), and an underlayment is recommended. We offer the STEICO underlayment, which is a great, sustainable, option on our website. But any underlayment meant for use with hardwood floors will work as long as it has a minimum compressive strength of (CS) > 60 kPa.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | What installation tools will I need?
settings.accordion_content:
We recommend using the following tools to complete your installation of Silvan:

  • Miter Saw & Table Saw
  • Tape Measure & T Square
  • Moisture Meter
  • White Glue (D3)
  • Straight Edge & 1/2” Spacers
  • Vapor Diffusion Retarder
  • PE Film
  • Chalk Line (Glue-Down)
  • Bona, Quantum R851 Adhesive (Glue-Down)

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | Can I install cabinets on top of my flooring?
settings.accordion_content:
It is always recommended to install cabinets before floating flooring, rather than installing cabinets on top of floating floors.

If you are planning to install your Silvan planks using the floating method, you will need to install your cabinets first. This lowers the risk of your floor failing due to insufficient expansion space in the future.

If you are planning to install the Silvan planks using the glue-down method, you can install cabinetry on top of the floor without concern.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | Can I install my flooring over an existing floor?
settings.accordion_content:
Silvan can be installed over most hard surfaces.

Silvan can be installed over most hard surfaces, including resilient floor coverings such as LVT, SPC, VCT, and linoleum, provided they are glued down, sufficiently fixed, completely level, and have no loose areas. The surface must be in good condition and show no signs of excessive moisture conditions.Do not install flooring over heavily cushioned floors such as rubber or cork.

Do not install over any type of carpet. The grout joints in ceramic tile and marble must be leveled so they are flush with the tile surface. Additionally, the tile may require several skim coats to achieve a flat surface.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | Can I install these planks on my wall?
settings.accordion_content: Yes! Silvan planks can be installed on walls. They can be installed both horizontally and vertically. You will need wall clips in order to install Silvan on your walls, though. These clips are not yet available on our website, but you can place an order for them over the phone. Please take a look at our Silvan Resilient Hardwood Wall Installation Instructions, found under the Technical Documents section of our website, for more information.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | Can I install these planks outdoors?
settings.accordion_content:
No. Our floors are designed for indoor use only.

The Silvan Collection, like all engineered wood products, is designed to be installed in temperature and moisture-controlled indoor environments.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | Can my flooring be installed over radiant heat?
settings.accordion_content:
The Silvan Collection is compatible with most radiant heating systems, provided that the temperature does not exceed 80 degrees Fahrenheit. The underfloor heating system must be flat and well-distributed in the subfloor.

We recommend covering the water-based floor heating systems with the pipes positioned in profiled particle floorboards with heat-distributing aluminum sheets and a tongue and groove particleboard or plywood that is at least 6 mm thick.

Please refer to our installation instructions for additional details and recommendations for installing Silvan planks over radiant heat systems.

Watch this video to learn more about installing your flooring over radiant heat!

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | Do you have a solution for stairs?
settings.accordion_content: Yes. We offer a round Nosing piece that is compatible with Silvan Engineered Hardwood planks. These can be used in combination with planks to form a tread.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | What kind of pattern should I use when laying the planks?
settings.accordion_content:
The ideal laying pattern is one that minimizes any kind of repetition and avoids "H" or "step" patterns.es any kind of repetition.

The pattern should be as random as possible, so seams (or "joints") do not catch the eye.

Three main patterns to avoid are close joints, "step" and "H" patterns. There are example images of "H" patterns and joints that are too close together in our installation instructions.

You can achieve an attractive install without too much effort by simply making sure the first piece you install in each row does not result in a close joint to the row before it (at least 16" apart), and that it doesn't line up with the joint two rows over.

If you're installing Silvan, getting the first plank in each row correct will ensure all the following planks line up correctly as well since all of the planks are the same length.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | How flat or level do I need my subfloor to be?
settings.accordion_content:
For our Silvan Collection, the official recommendation for subfloor flatness is that any imperfections should not exceed 1/16" over 6'.

More than levelness, "flatness" is a much more important factor. In other words, if your entire room slopes in one direction, but is otherwise flat the entire way, your installation can be successful.

For our Silvan Collection, the official recommendation for subfloor flatness is that any imperfections should not exceed 1/16" over 6'.

That being said, we have had many customers tell us they have installed on considerably less flat surfaces. There are a couple of concerns with the subfloor not being flat:

The first is that the click mechanism may come loose. If the subfloor changes angle too dramatically in the middle of a plank, the pressure over time may lead to the click mechanism breaking or coming loose.

The other concern is hollowness. When a plank bridges a valley, the hollow spots can result in the floor sounding soft or "loose" wherever there are air pockets between the floor and the subfloor.
Checking for flatness prior to your installation is the most important step you can take for a successful install.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | How long does the floor need to acclimate before it is installed?
settings.accordion_content: Silvan planks require 48 hours to acclimate before installation.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | How many clips do I need when installing the planks on a wall?
settings.accordion_content:
You will need about one 5G Climb clip per square foot, but we recommend ordering extra if your wall has windows

How many clips you need to complete your Silvan wall installation depends on several factors, including the dimensions of your walls, and the number and placement of any windows. As a general rule, you will need approximately one 5G Climb clip per square foot if your wall has no windows. If your wall does have windows, you'll want to order another 10 or so per window. Each box of 5G Climb clips contains 40 clips.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | What can I do to minimize or avoid the appearance of pattern repetition?
settings.accordion_content:
Because Silvan planks include a real oak wear layer, no two planks will be exactly the same. We still recommend opening 2-3 boxes at a time when installing your floor to ensure that you can achieve the look you want.

Unlike LVP, which is made using print films and has repeating grain patterns, engineered wood floors like our Silvan Collection have a layer of real wood, so every plank will be unique. That being said, you will sometimes find planks made using wood from the same part of a particular tree. This results in two planks that have a very similar grain pattern. While it isn't a true "repeat" like you get with vinyl flooring, it is still desirable to arrange your planks so that these similar planks aren't too close to each other.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | How do I care for my floor?
settings.accordion_content:
After installing the floor, we recommend an initial cleaning to remove any loose dirt or debris that may have been introduced during the installation process. Any products that are safe to use on UV acrylic wear layer hardwood floors will be suitable. We recommend Bona Hardwood Flooret Cleaner or any similar brand. While most non-residue cleaners can be used on your engineered wood floor, it is always recommended to conduct a small test patch in an inconspicuous area if you choose to use a different type of cleaner, and avoid using harsh cleaners or ammonia-based cleaning products.

Keep Floors Clean

Regularly sweep and vacuum your floors. Dust acts as an abrasive. Keeping your floors dust-free will prolong the life of your finish and wear-layer. Use a vacuum that is suitable for hard surface floors.Use walk-off mats at outside entrances to reduce the amount of dirt brought into your home.

As a general rule of thumb, the heavier the item, the wider the floor protector is needed. We recommend felt pads at least 1” in diameter.Be careful with rolling casters. They can damage the floor. If you choose to use them, look for the widest possible wheel you can find.

Sunlight Exposure

Most flooring will eventually fade when exposed to UV. To keep your floors in pristine condition, avoid exposure to direct sunlight for prolonged periods of time. During peak sunlight hours, use drapes or blinds to minimize the direct sunlight on the vinyl flooring.In addition, excessive temperatures are not good for resilient floors. Some natural ventilation or intermittent air conditioning in vacant homes should be considered. Long-term continuous inside temperatures over 80°F combined with strong direct sunlight will damage the flooring and cause the installation to fail.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | What is the best cleaner to use on my floors?
settings.accordion_content:
Any products that are safe to use on UV acrylic wear layer hardwood floors will be suitable. We recommend Bona Hardwood Flooret Cleaner or any similar brand. When you mop the floor, make sure the solution is absorbed within one minute.

Use Hardwood Floor Cleaner specially developed for UV Acrylic Wear Layer Hardwood floors. Normal soap may form a coating on the surface which makes the floor more difficult to clean.

We recommend mainly using dry cleaning methods, such as a vacuum cleaner, dust mop or microfiber mop.

If you do get a stain on your flooring, make sure to remove it as quickly as possible as instructed below. No warranties apply if using strong stain removal agents in large amounts and/or rubbing the surface excessively.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | What temperature and humidity range is suitable for my floor?
settings.accordion_content:
After installation, the floor has a temperature tolerance range of 50°F - 85°F, and relative air humidity (RH) tolerance range of 35 - 65%.

Wood has hygroscopic characteristics, meaning it moves with natural changes of relative humidity: in the summer it normally swells and in winter it normally shrinks. When the wood shrinks, natural gaps between the boards appear. To prevent excessive movement and consequential damage to the floor, the indoor climate should have a temperature between 50° and 85°F and relative air humidity (RH) between 35 - 65%.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | Will sun exposure damage my floor?
settings.accordion_content: Most flooring will eventually fade when exposed to UV. To keep your floors in pristine condition, avoid exposure to direct sunlight for prolonged periods of time. During peak sunlight hours, use drapes or blinds to minimize the direct sunlight on the flooring.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | What do I do if my house experiences flooding?
settings.accordion_content:
The Silvan Collection is topically waterproof, but if water gets under the planks, you will likely need to replace them.

If you spill water on your floor, do not panic; our Silvan Collection is topically waterproof. This means that the surface of the planks will not be adversely affected by water and the seams are 100% watertight. If the water did not reach the perimeter of the installation, simply remove it as quickly as possible. Take a look at this video which shows how water can sit on the surface of the planks for at least 24 hours without harming the surface or seeping through.

Depending on the extent of the flooding, you may need to replace the affected planks. You can use a 5G Tool to disengage the end to end drop click mechanism.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | What rugs and rug pads can I safely use with your floor?
settings.accordion_content: Any rug that is safe to use on UV-cured acrylic coated engineered hardwood floors will be safe to use on our Silvan Collection. Rugs made from wool, cotton, and other natural fibers will be safe. Rug pads made from natural rubber are also safe, but you'll want to avoid rubber containing added glues and adhesives. We recommend contacting the manufacturer of the rug or rug pad to ensure that the product you are considering is safe to use on UV-cured acrylic coated engineered hardwood floors.

settings.accordion_title: Silvan | How do I replace a plank?
settings.accordion_content:
If needed, you can replace a Silvan plank in the interior of your installation.

Take a look atthis video, which does a great job of showing how to replace one of our Silvan planks.
